annotations.title: Open a JDG in Poland: tax forms and steps

description: Compares the three income tax forms for a new Polish sole proprietorship (JDG) for 2026: progressive scale, flat tax and lump-sum tax (ryczałt), each with social ZUS, health contribution, PIT and net income, from monthly revenue and costs and the founder's ZUS situation. Also returns the CEIDG, tax form, ZUS and VAT steps, what Norman does next (the details for the CEIDG-1, which the founder signs and sends) and continueInNorman, a link that opens Norman's JDG planner with these answers. situation: new = no business in the last 60 months and no work for a former employer (ulga na start, then preferential ZUS); recent = a business in the last 60 months (full ZUS); employment = also employed at least at the minimum wage (health contribution only); former_employer = the same work for this or last year's employer (full ZUS, ryczałt not available). Without lumpSumRate the ryczałt row is left out. Figures only: nothing is saved, and the result is general information without a recommendation of a tax form or ZUS scheme, not legal or tax advice. The inputs hold no personal data.

city.description: City of the business in Poland.

companyName.description: Business name (firma) the founder plans, if any.

idea.description: The user's business idea in their own words.

lumpSumRate.description: Ryczałt rate in percent that applies to the activity; without it the ryczałt row is left out.

monthlyCosts.description: Expected monthly business costs in złoty, net of VAT.

monthlyRevenue.description: Expected monthly revenue in złoty, net of VAT.

situation.description: The founder's ZUS situation: new, recent, employment or former_employer.

year.description: Year of the rules and rates: 2026.
